note: The Agent Skills specification defines six frontmatter fields: `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, and `allowed-tools`. Those six are portable and stay at the top level everywhere. Every other key is one product's extension, so it carries a placement per harness: `top-level` where the harness reads it, `metadata` where it does not, since `metadata` is the map the specification reserves for exactly that. Neither harness rejects an unknown key — the Codex parser ignores anything outside `name`, `description`, and `metadata.short-description` — so placement is about writing only what a harness asked for, not about avoiding a crash. Codex UI, invocation policy, and tool dependencies belong in `agents/openai.yaml`, never in frontmatter. Revisit when either product documents a key it does not read today.

metadata_namespaces.references: Reference documents the skill loads, keyed by path relative to the declaring file.
metadata_namespaces.agents: Agent definitions the skill delegates to, keyed by path relative to the declaring file.
metadata_namespaces.skills: Other skills this one invokes, keyed by plugin-qualified or bare name.
metadata_namespaces.config: The skill's own runtime defaults, such as an output directory.

forms.verbatim: Portable key the author writes literally in frontmatter; the renderer places nothing.
forms.plain-scalar: Space-separated string written unquoted; a list argument joins with spaces and a value that would not survive as a plain YAML scalar fails the build.
forms.quoted-scalar: Single line written double-quoted with its own quotes escaped; a line break fails the build.
forms.placeholder-names: Space-separated names that can each spell a `$name` placeholder; any other name fails the build.

name.intent: Skill identifier, and the slash command that invokes it.

description.intent: What the skill does and when to use it; both harnesses trigger on it.

allowed-tools.intent: Tools the assistant may use without asking permission during the invoking turn.

Codex.note: Specification field, marked experimental; Codex accepts it and does not enforce it as a permission rule.

argument-hint.intent: Hint shown during autocomplete to indicate the expected arguments.

Codex.note: Not a Codex frontmatter control. The parser reads `name`, `description`, and `metadata.short-description` only, and ignores everything else.

arguments.intent: Named positional arguments, substituted as `$name` in the skill body.

Codex.note: Codex documents no argument substitution, so a body that spells a placeholder does it inside a harness conditional.

license.intent: License covering the skill, as a name or a bundled file reference.

Codex.note: Portable specification metadata; Codex does not use it during execution.

compatibility.intent: Environment the skill needs: intended product, system packages, network access.

Codex.note: Portable specification metadata; Codex does not enforce it.

short-description.intent: Short label shown beside the skill in a product's own surface.

ClaudeCode.note: Claude Code reads no short label; the entry rides along inert.

Codex.note: The one nested key the Codex parser reads, defined as a `metadata` sub-key rather than a top-level one.
